subject: MSA / Order Form: security exhibit governance — SOC 2 assertions, pen-test gating, evidence cadence
messages:
From: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@wellpath.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Rios <maria.rios@wellpath.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit questions + SOC2 evidence cadence

Hi Grace —

Thanks for sending the draft order form last week. Our legal team has a few specific asks on the security exhibit:

1) Can you confirm which SOC 2 assertions Redwood is willing to commit to in the exhibit (Confidentiality, Availability, Processing Integrity)?
2) For pen testing — we need to understand the notice window and whether staging access is required or if a remote summary is acceptable.
3) Evidence cadence — we prefer a quarterly evidence bundle (logs, patching attestations, and monthly SOC2 evidence snapshots). Is that something Redwood can support?

Uploading a short summary of our preferred cadence — attaching a sample internal checklist.

Appreciate a quick sync this week if possible.

Thanks,
Ethan
Security Lead, WellPath Health
(attachment: wellpath-evidence-checklist.pdf)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@wellpath.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions + SOC2 evidence cadence

Ethan —

Really appreciate the clear asks. I pulled in Karthik (legal) and Connor (security ops) to confirm feasibility. High level responses below; I also attached a marked-up security exhibit (redlines-security-exhibit-v1.pdf) with proposed language.

- SOC 2: Redwood is comfortable committing to Availability and Confidentiality assertions in the exhibit; Processing Integrity language is negotiable depending on the Order Form class (we can scope specific service-level statements).
- Pen test: default cadence is annual + ad-hoc with 30 days notice for non-production testing. For customers requiring staging access, we can provide ephemeral staging credentials during a pre-approved window — otherwise we accept a third-party summary and evidence package if the tester cannot access staging.
- Evidence cadence: quarterly full-bundles are fine. We typically provide quarterly evidence bundles and a rolling monthly snapshot for operational metrics (uptime, incident summaries). We can map your requested items to our standard artifact list.

Next steps I propose: 1) Karthik to review the redline language and call out any legal must-haves; 2) Connor to propose a pen-test gating matrix (staging vs summary) and a sample window schedule; 3) sync call Thurs 11am PT to finalize Order Form carveouts.

If that works, I'll attach the draft pen-test windows spreadsheet and the SOC 2 attest report (for your internal review).

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
(attachments: redlines-security-exhibit-v1.pdf; wellpath-pen-test-windows.xlsx; soc2-2027-certified.pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@wellpath.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions + SOC2 evidence cadence

Ethan / Grace / team —

Thanks for the context. Quick legal notes after a first pass on the attached redlines:

- SOC 2 assertions: we will retain Availability and Confidentiality commitments; for Processing Integrity, propose a service-level carveout ("processing integrity subject to customer supplied input validation and limits") — happy to draft exact clause.
- Pen test language: we need to keep an indemnity-safe harbor for ephemeral staging access (limited scope, supervised sessions, no exploitation of PII). We'll add required scope-limiting language and an escalation path if the tester identifies a finding that requires hotfixing outside the normal cadence.
- Evidence cadence: quarterly bundles are acceptable; however, we need to limit retention obligations to artifacts Redwood controls. For customer-provided telemetry we can document the handoff process but not assume retention responsibility.

I'll attach inline comments in the PDF. If WellPath's counsel wants different indemnity or escrow terms we'll escalate, but this is a productive baseline. Happy to take questions on the Thurs call.

Karthik
VP Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
(attachment referenced: redlines-security-exhibit-v1.pdf - legal comments)

From: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@wellpath.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Rios <maria.rios@wellpath.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions + SOC2 evidence cadence

Karthik / Grace —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and annotated redlines. A few clarifications from our side:

- Processing Integrity: we can live with the carveout if the Order Form includes a short SLA for request validation and an incident reprocessing commitment (48 hours for critical data misprocessing).
- Pen test indemnity: our counsel is typically okay with supervised staging access and limited indemnity but asked if Redwood can shorten the notice window to 21 days for critical regulatory customers.
- Evidence retention: we will own customer-side telemetry; the quarterly bundle request is primarily for SOC 2 artifacts and patch/scan summaries.

We prefer to review Karthik's marked-up PDF before the call — can you share the inline comments as a flattened doc or Google Doc?

Thanks,
Ethan

Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions + SOC2 evidence cadence

Ethan —

Thanks — noted on the 21 day request. Connor and I discussed the staging access tradeoffs: we can offer a shortened 21-day notice for customers with regulatory constraints if the Order Form includes a scoped attacker profile and a one-time supervised window (no more than 48 hours). We'll add that as an optional Order Form checkbox.

Karthik will export the PDF comments to a Google Doc and share the link (I included it in related_links above). Attached is an updated pen-test windows sheet that maps "standard" vs "regulated" workflows and the proposed scheduling lanes.

If that aligns, let's use the Thurs 11am PT call to sign off on the exact exhibit language and push the redline into the procurement queue. Agenda for the call: 1) confirm SOC2 assertions line; 2) finalize pen-test notice window and staging rules; 3) agree evidence bundle items and delivery cadence; 4) procurement next steps and signature timeline.

Best,
Grace
